# Aetherix White Papers — benchmark results

> LLM and CV inference benchmarks: which model runs on which NVIDIA device, how fast, and for how many users or cameras.

Explorers: https://whitepapers.aetherix.com/llm-inference-benchmarks/ · https://whitepapers.aetherix.com/cv-inference-benchmarks/
Raw data: https://whitepapers.aetherix.com/assets/data/benchmarks.json · https://whitepapers.aetherix.com/assets/data/cv-benchmarks/index.json
Please cite the explorer page, not this file. Each record's link opens that run in the interactive table.

## LLM inference benchmarks

Each entry below describes one serving configuration — a model on one device, in one number format, with one engine and one parallelism and speculative-decoding setting — measured with the open-source CordatusAI LLM Benchmark Tool (128 input and 128 output tokens, prompts on different topics, ten rounds at each concurrency level C = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, mean values). Max C is the highest measured concurrency meeting both targets; the capacity figures turn it into people and check it against the KV cache memory, taking the smaller of the two limits. Capacity is an estimate, not a measurement, and no substitute for a production load test. The Intelligence and Agentic Index values in the interactive table come from Artificial Analysis. The chat and agentic capacity estimates are the two ends of a range: for coding- and agent-heavy use the realistic figure is closer to the agentic estimate, for simple question-and-answer use closer to the chat estimate.

Defaults used below: TTFT ≤ 1000 ms, TPS ≥ 20 tok/s per request; chat sessions 16384 tokens, speed × 4; agentic sessions 65536 tokens, speed × 1.5. Capacity = min(speed limit, KV cache memory limit); "+" = the run never failed the targets, so the figure is a minimum.

### GPT-OSS 120B · 1× DGX Spark · MXFP4 · vLLM

- link: https://whitepapers.aetherix.com/llm-inference-benchmarks/#gpt-oss-120b_1spark_mxfp4_vllm
- model: GPT-OSS 120B; parameters: 120B; checkpoint: https://huggingface.co/openai/gpt-oss-120b
- setup: 1× DGX Spark, MXFP4, vLLM, TP=1, DP=1, PP=1, speculative decoding: no
- measured (C = concurrent requests; TTFT / per-request TPS): C=1: 220 ms / 55.65 tok/s; C=2: 294 ms / 37.05 tok/s; C=4: 321 ms / 25.2 tok/s; C=8: 395 ms / 16.88 tok/s; C=16: 444 ms / 11.67 tok/s; C=32: 552 ms / 8.26 tok/s
- Max C: 4
- chat capacity (users): 16, limited by speed
- agentic capacity (users): 6, limited by speed
- In this measurement, GPT-OSS 120B (120B parameters), served in MXFP4 format with vLLM on 1× DGX Spark, reached a generation speed of 55.6 tok/s per request and a time to first token (TTFT) of 220 ms with a single request. Considering the speed targets and the available KV cache capacity, the estimated capacity is 16 users for chat use and 6 for agentic use. The realistic capacity will likely fall between these two values. In scenarios dominated by coding, tool use, long workflows and multi-agent use, capacity approaches the agentic estimate; where shorter interactions, standard conversations and lighter tasks dominate, it approaches the chat estimate.

### GPT-OSS 120B · 2× DGX Spark · MXFP4 · vLLM

- link: https://whitepapers.aetherix.com/llm-inference-benchmarks/#gpt-oss-120b_2spark_mxfp4_vllm
- model: GPT-OSS 120B; parameters: 120B; checkpoint: https://huggingface.co/openai/gpt-oss-120b
- setup: 2× DGX Spark, MXFP4, vLLM, TP=2, DP=1, PP=1, speculative decoding: no
- measured (C = concurrent requests; TTFT / per-request TPS): C=1: 168 ms / 69.86 tok/s; C=2: 228 ms / 51.52 tok/s; C=4: 255 ms / 37.14 tok/s; C=8: 292 ms / 26.92 tok/s; C=16: 320 ms / 19.08 tok/s; C=32: 465 ms / 12.63 tok/s
- Max C: 8
- chat capacity (users): 32, limited by speed
- agentic capacity (users): 12, limited by speed
- In this measurement, GPT-OSS 120B (120B parameters), served in MXFP4 format with vLLM on 2× DGX Spark (TP=2), reached a generation speed of 69.9 tok/s per request and a time to first token (TTFT) of 168 ms with a single request. Considering the speed targets and the available KV cache capacity, the estimated capacity is 32 users for chat use and 12 for agentic use. The realistic capacity will likely fall between these two values. In scenarios dominated by coding, tool use, long workflows and multi-agent use, capacity approaches the agentic estimate; where shorter interactions, standard conversations and lighter tasks dominate, it approaches the chat estimate.

Considering the speed targets and the available KV cache capacity, the estimated capacity is 55 users for chat use and 13 for agentic use. The realistic capacity will likely fall between these two values. In scenarios dominated by coding, tool use, long workflows and multi-agent use, capacity approaches the agentic estimate; where shorter interactions, standard conversations and lighter tasks dominate, it approaches the chat estimate.

At the default speed targets (at least 20 tok/s per request, TTFT at most 1,000 ms) there is no capacity estimate for this configuration: no measured load level met them.

- model: GLM-4.7; parameters: 358B
- setup: DGX B300, NVFP4, vLLM, TP=1, DP=1, PP=1, speculative decoding: no
- measured (C = concurrent requests; TTFT / per-request TPS): C=1: 157 ms / 63.87 tok/s; C=2: 273 ms / 55.84 tok/s; C=4: 256 ms / 50.54 tok/s; C=8: 286 ms / 42.35 tok/s; C=16: 324 ms / 35.44 tok/s; C=32: 393 ms / 29.24 tok/s
- Max C: 32+
- chat capacity (users): 21, limited by KV cache memory
- agentic capacity (users): 5, limited by KV cache memory
- In this measurement, GLM-4.7 (358B parameters), served in NVFP4 format with vLLM on DGX B300, reached a generation speed of 63.9 tok/s per request and a time to first token (TTFT) of 157 ms with a single request. Considering the speed targets and the available KV cache capacity, the estimated capacity is 21 users for chat use and 5 for agentic use. The realistic capacity will likely fall between these two values. In scenarios dominated by coding, tool use, long workflows and multi-agent use, capacity approaches the agentic estimate; where shorter interactions, standard conversations and lighter tasks dominate, it approaches the chat estimate.

## CV inference benchmarks

Each entry below describes one deployment configuration — one detection model, at one precision and input resolution, on one device, running on the Cordatus Inference Engine over DeepStream — measured with the cordatus-benchmark tool against live 1080p H.264 IP cameras streaming a fixed 20 FPS, with 30 seconds of steady-state sampling at each camera count. Max cameras is the highest measured camera count that still holds the target frame rate per camera; nothing is extrapolated. These are speed measurements only, and no substitute for a test on your own cameras.

### PeopleNet INT8 · GB10

- link: https://whitepapers.aetherix.com/cv-inference-benchmarks/
- model: PeopleNet; precision: INT8; input resolution: 960x544; device: GB10
- measured (cameras: FPS per camera, frame drop): 1 cam: 19.88 FPS/cam, drop 0.43%; 2 cam: 20.34 FPS/cam, drop -2.5%; 4 cam: 20.11 FPS/cam, drop -1.36%; 8 cam: 20.01 FPS/cam, drop -0.66%; 10 cam: 19.39 FPS/cam, drop -0.04%; 12 cam: 19.42 FPS/cam, drop 0.03%; 14 cam: 19.5 FPS/cam, drop -0.27%; 16 cam: 19.49 FPS/cam, drop 0.02%; 18 cam: 19.6 FPS/cam, drop 0.22%; 20 cam: 19.59 FPS/cam, drop 0.08%; 22 cam: 19.57 FPS/cam, drop 0.51%; 24 cam: 19.66 FPS/cam, drop 0.69%; 26 cam: 19.0 FPS/cam, drop 0.12%; 28 cam: 17.63 FPS/cam, drop 0.65%; 30 cam: 15.54 FPS/cam, drop -1.07%; 32 cam: 14.13 FPS/cam, drop 0.55%
- Max cameras at the default 15.0 FPS per camera: 30
- In this measurement, PeopleNet INT8 (960x544 input) on GB10, at its heaviest measured load of 32 cameras, processed 14.1 FPS per camera and 452.1 FPS in total, with 0.6% frame drop. At the default target of 15 FPS per camera, the highest measured camera count that holds it (Max cameras) is 30.
